steps.message:
# RL training run diagnosis

Review the staged post-training experiment and determine whether it is healthy
or unhealthy. Treat the workspace as a historical snapshot: inspect its source,
effective configuration, launch scripts, data, reward logic, and any logs or
metrics that are present. Do not assume that an unusual setting or
implementation is causal without connecting it to observed behavior.

Use held-out evaluation evidence together with rollout, truncation, runtime,
optimization, and training signals. Training reward alone does not establish
held-out health. A truncated log is not by itself proof of a defect.

Do not launch a full training run, use the network, or modify the historical
snapshot. The dataset, held-out set, model, training-step budget, and evaluation
interval are fixed.

## Deliverable

Write one concise UTF-8 diagnosis to:

```text
$PTDBENCH_RESULTS/agent_answer.md
```

State the verdict, identify the concrete root cause or causes, and explain the
causal chain using specific workspace evidence. Distinguish root causes from
symptoms. Do not propose or implement a fix, and do not write other deliverable
files.
I'll start by exploring the workspace to understand the experiment structure, then systematically diagnose the training run.

# -------------------------------
# build-system
# -------------------------------
[build-system]
requires = [
    "setuptools>=61.0",
    "wheel"
]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

# -------------------------------
# project (PEP 621 metadata)
# -------------------------------
[project]
name = "verl"
# We'll mark the version as "dynamic" because it's read from the file "verl/version/version" 
# (PEP 621 calls this "dynamic version"). 
# The actual version is specified in the [tool.setuptools.dynamic] section below.
dynamic = ["version", "dependencies", "optional-dependencies", "authors", "urls"]

description = "verl: Volcano Engine Reinforcement Learning for LLM"
license = {text = "Apache-2.0"}  # Changed from file to text format
readme = {file = "README.md", content-type = "text/markdown"}
requires-python = ">=3.10"

# -------------------------------
# tool.ruff - Linting configuration
# -------------------------------
[tool.ruff]
# Note: While the formatter will attempt to format lines such that they remain within the line-length,
# it isn't a hard upper bound, and formatted lines may exceed the line-length.
line-length = 120
exclude = ["scripts/legacy_model_merger.py"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
isort = {known-first-party = ["verl"]}
# c.f. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/ce8d6b75fc0586045df75ee1568a5b5f9957251b/pyproject.toml
select = [
    # pycodestyle
    "E",
    # Pyflakes
    "F",
    # pyupgrade
    "UP",
    # flake8-bugbear
    "B",
    # isort
    "I",
    "G",
]
ignore = [
    # star imports
    "F405", "F403",
    # lambda expression assignment
    "E731",
    # Loop control variable not used within loop body
    "B007",
    # f-string format
    "UP032",
    # `.log()` statement uses f-string
    "G004",
    # X | None for type annotations
    "UP045",
    # deprecated import
    "UP035",
]

# -------------------------------
# tool.mypy - typechecking config
# -------------------------------
[tool.mypy]
pretty            = true
ignore_missing_imports = true
explicit_package_bases = true
follow_imports = "skip"

# Blanket silence
ignore_errors = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
"verl.trainer.config.algorithm",
"verl.trainer.ppo.core_algos",
"verl.trainer.ppo.reward",
"verl.workers.reward_manager",
"verl.workers.reward_manager.*",
]
ignore_errors = false

# -------------------------------
# tool.setuptools - Additional config
# -------------------------------
[tool.setuptools]
# True means `setuptools` will attempt to include all relevant files in package_data automatically.
# This corresponds to `include_package_data=True` in setup.py.
include-package-data = true

# We read the version from a file in 'verl/version/version'
[tool.setuptools.dynamic]
version = {file = "verl/version/version"}

# If you need to mimic `package_dir={'': '.'}`:
[tool.setuptools.package-dir]
"" = "."

# If you need to include specific non-Python data (like YAML files or version file):
# This is the rough equivalent of package_data={'': ['version/*'], 'verl': ['trainer/config/*.yaml']}
[tool.setuptools.package-data]
verl = [
  "version/*",
  "trainer/config/*.yaml",
  "trainer/config/*/*.yaml",
  "experimental/*/config/*.yaml",
]

# setup.py is the fallback installation script when pyproject.toml does not work
import os
from pathlib import Path

from setuptools import find_packages, setup

version_folder = os.path.dirname(os.path.join(os.path.abspath(__file__)))

with open(os.path.join(version_folder, "verl/version/version")) as f:
    __version__ = f.read().strip()

install_requires = [
    "accelerate",
    "codetiming",
    "datasets",
    "dill",
    "hydra-core",
    "numpy>=2.0.0",
    "pandas",
    "peft",
    "pyarrow>=19.0.0",
    "pybind11",
    "pylatexenc",
    "ray[default]>=2.41.0",
    "torchdata",
    "tensordict>=0.8.0,<=0.10.0,!=0.9.0",
    # 5.6.0 ships a broken flash-attention path (crashes on s_aux=None for
    # sink-less models); fixed in 5.6.1. See huggingface/transformers#45588.
    "transformers!=5.6.0",
    "wandb",
    "packaging>=20.0",
    "tensorboard",
]

TEST_REQUIRES = ["pytest", "pre-commit", "py-spy", "pytest-asyncio", "pytest-rerunfailures"]
PRIME_REQUIRES = ["pyext"]
GEO_REQUIRES = ["mathruler", "torchvision", "qwen_vl_utils"]
GPU_REQUIRES = ["liger-kernel", "flash-attn"]
MATH_REQUIRES = ["math-verify"]  # Add math-verify as an optional dependency
VLLM_REQUIRES = ["tensordict>=0.8.0,<=0.10.0,!=0.9.0", "vllm>=0.8.5,<=0.12.0"]
TRTLLM_REQUIRES = ["tensorrt-llm>=1.2.0rc6"]
SGLANG_REQUIRES = [
    "tensordict>=0.8.0,<=0.10.0,!=0.9.0",
    "sglang[srt,openai]==0.5.8",
    "torch==2.9.1",
]
TRL_REQUIRES = ["trl<=0.9.6"]
# Keep the legacy mbridge dependency available during its deprecation window.
MCORE_REQUIRES = ["megatron-bridge", "mbridge"]

extras_require = {
    "test": TEST_REQUIRES,
    "prime": PRIME_REQUIRES,
    "geo": GEO_REQUIRES,
    "gpu": GPU_REQUIRES,
    "math": MATH_REQUIRES,
    "vllm": VLLM_REQUIRES,
    "sglang": SGLANG_REQUIRES,
    "trl": TRL_REQUIRES,
    "mcore": MCORE_REQUIRES,
    "trtllm": TRTLLM_REQUIRES,
}


this_directory = Path(__file__).parent
long_description = (this_directory / "README.md").read_text()

setup(
    name="verl",
    version=__version__,
    package_dir={"": "."},
    packages=find_packages(where="."),
    url="https://github.com/verl-project/verl",
    license="Apache 2.0",
    author="Bytedance - Seed - MLSys",
    author_email="zhangchi.usc1992@bytedance.com, gmsheng@connect.hku.hk",
    description="verl: Volcano Engine Reinforcement Learning for LLM",
    install_requires=install_requires,
    extras_require=extras_require,
    package_data={
        "": ["version/*"],
        "verl": [
            "trainer/config/*.yaml",
            "trainer/config/*/*.yaml",
            "experimental/*/config/*.yaml",
        ],
    },
    include_package_data=True,
    long_description=long_description,
    long_description_content_type="text/markdown",
)

import json, glob

# Check if data_source values explain score behavior
# Since it's GRPO with binary reward, check how many distinct problems in the batch
# The batch size 16 means each step samples 16 prompts from train set. With N=2329 training problems,
# the chance any single step has a positive reward is ~ probability a sampled problem has at least 1 positive rollout

# Let's check rollout data: per step, what fraction of the 128 rollouts (16 prompts x 8) are positive
import os
files=sorted(glob.glob('rollout_data/*.jsonl'), key=lambda x: int(x.split('/')[-1].split('.')[0]))
tot_pos=0
pos_any=0
tot_steps=len(files)
for f in files:
    with open(f) as fh:
        lines=[json.loads(l) for l in fh]
        pos_this=sum(1 for l in lines if l['score']>0)
        tot_pos += pos_this
        if pos_this > 0:
            pos_any += 1

print(f'total positive rollouts: {tot_pos} / {tot_steps*128} = {tot_pos/(tot_steps*128*128):.6f}')
print(f'steps with any positive: {pos_any} / {tot_steps} = {pos_any/tot_steps:.3f}')
# Also: per-problem pass rate
from collections import Counter
prob_pos=Counter()
for f in files:
    with open(f) as fh:
        for line in fh:
            d=json.loads(line)
            # extract some problem id from input text - use first 50 chars of the QUESTION part
            inp=d.get('input','')
            if 'QUESTION:' in inp:
                qid=inp.split('QUESTION:',1)[1][:80]
            else:
                qid=inp[:80]
            if d['score']>0:
                prob_pos[qid]+=1
print('distinct problem-ids seen:', len(prob_pos))
print('top 5 by positive count:', prob_pos.most_common(5))
"

python3 -I -c "
import json

# Check batch: 16 prompts per step, train set 2329 items, so problems repeat 
# every ~2329/16 ≈ 145 steps. Let's compute reward per unique problem.
import glob, collections

rollouts={}
for f in glob.glob('rollout_data/*.jsonl'):
    step=int(f.split('/')[-1].split('.')[0])
    with open(f) as fh:
        for line in fh:
            d=json.loads(line)
            inp=d.get('input','')
            if 'QUESTION:' in inp:
                qid=inp.split('QUESTION:',1)[1].split(chr(10))[0][:120]
            else:
                qid=inp[:120]
            rollouts.setdefault(step,[]).append((qid, d['score']))

# For each step compute: mean score, fraction of problems with at least one positive rollout
per_step=[]
for step in sorted(rollouts):
    items=rollouts[step]
    # group by qid
    by_qid=collections.defaultdict(list)
    for qid,score in items:
        by_qid[qid].append(score)
    n_probs=len(by_qid)  # should be ~16
    n_any_pos=sum(1 for scores in by_qid.values() if max(scores)>0)
    step_mean=sum(s for _,s in items)/len(items)
    per_step.append((step, step_mean, n_probs, n_any_pos))

print('first 10 steps: (step, step_mean, n_problems, n_any_positive)')
for x in per_step[:10]:
    print(x)
print('last 5 steps:')
for x in per_step[-5:]:
    print(x)
zero_mean=sum(1 for s,smean,_,_ in per_step if smean==0)
print(f'steps with zero mean score: {zero_mean} / {len(per_step)}')
"

# Wait - n_probs=1 per step smells wrong. Each rollout file has batch_size * rollout_n entries.
# batch=16, rollout_n=8 => 128 entries per step file. 
# But each entry appears to use same qid? Let's check.

# Actually the input is a long chat template. Let's just count how many unique input texts per file.

for f in ['rollout_data/1.jsonl','rollout_data/2.jsonl','rollout_data/3.jsonl']:
    with open(f) as fh:
        data=[json.loads(l) for l in fh]
    inputs=[d['input'] for d in data]
    # Use first 200 chars
    short=[i[:200] for i in inputs]
    unique=set(short)
    print(f'{f}: {len(data)} entries, {len(unique)} unique prompts')
    # show their scores
    scores=[d['score'] for d in data]
    print(f'  scores: {sorted(Counter(round(s,6) for s in scores).most_common())}')
"

def compute_grpo_outcome_advantage(
    token_level_rewards: torch.Tensor,
    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
    index: np.ndarray,
    epsilon: float = 1e-6,
    norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo: bool = True,
    config: Optional[AlgoConfig] = None,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """
    Compute advantage for GRPO, operating only on Outcome reward
    (with only one scalar reward for each response).

    Args:
        token_level_rewards: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape is (bs, response_length)
        response_mask: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape is (bs, response_length)
        index: `(np.ndarray)`
            index array for grouping
        epsilon: `(float)`
            small value to avoid division by zero
        norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo: `(bool)`
            whether to scale the GRPO advantage
        config: `(Optional[AlgoConfig])`
            algorithm configuration object

    Note:
        If norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo is True, the advantage is scaled by the std, as in the original GRPO.
        If False, the advantage is not scaled, as in Dr.GRPO (https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.20783).

    Returns:
        advantages: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape is (bs, response_length)
        Returns: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape is (bs, response_length)
    """
    scores = token_level_rewards.sum(dim=-1)

    id2score = defaultdict(list)
    id2mean = {}
    id2std = {}

    with torch.no_grad():
        bsz = scores.shape[0]
        for i in range(bsz):
            id2score[index[i]].append(scores[i])
        for idx in id2score:
            if len(id2score[idx]) == 1:
                id2mean[idx] = torch.tensor(0.0)
                id2std[idx] = torch.tensor(1.0)
            elif len(id2score[idx]) > 1:
                scores_tensor = torch.stack(id2score[idx])
                id2mean[idx] = torch.mean(scores_tensor)
                id2std[idx] = torch.std(scores_tensor)
            else:
                raise ValueError(f"no score in prompt index: {idx}")
        for i in range(bsz):
            if norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo:
                scores[i] = (scores[i] - id2mean[index[i]]) / (id2std[index[i]] + epsilon)
            else:
                scores[i] = scores[i] - id2mean[index[i]]
        scores = scores.unsqueeze(-1) * response_mask

    return scores, scores

steps.reasoning_content:
Final numbers are now crisp. Let me summarize my findings into a comprehensive root-cause picture:

**The core problem: ~95% of the training data yields zero reward, and the ~5% that does yields 0.78% positive rollouts → GRPO advantage is almost always exactly zero → no learning signal → no held-out improvement.**

Key figures:
- Train: 2329 problems; 2151 distinct sampled in 400 steps (batch 16, so 6400 prompt-samples; some problems sampled multiple times).
- Of 6400 prompt-samples (16/step), only 2.73% ever contain a mixed pass/fail signal.
- 399/51200 = 0.78% rollouts pass (TACO pass@1 for the base Qwen2.5-1.5B on this CodeForces-heavy hard set).
- 62.3% of groups all-fail, so advantage = 0.
- Even the 4.8% "solvable" problems only pass ~0.8% of their 8 samples.

**The mechanism that makes it all-crash together:**
1. Binary reward (compute_score → score=binary, from taco.py's compute_score returning `binary`). The pass_rate signal (0.22 vs acc 0.07) is computed and logged but NOT used as reward — discarded.
2. GRPO computes advantage via group std normalization. When a group is all-0 (or all-1), std≈0, advantage is 0 (and clamps with epsilon). So 97%+ of groups produce zero advantage.
3. Additionally, `actor/entropy:0.69` initially and `pg_loss:0.0` for 256/400 steps AND ppl_ratio ~1.0006, rollout_corr/kl ~0.0006 (essentially no policy drift), combined with grad_norm tiny (~0.005-0.1).
4. Internal train score mean 0.0078 (flat, no trend).

**What the mixed evidence would otherwise attribute (symptoms, NOT root causes):**
- The held-out validation flattens (7.06% → 7.61%, noise). This is a symptom.
- pg_loss == 0 for 256/400 steps (symptom of zero advantage).
- No policy drift (KL ~ 0.0006, ppl_ratio ~ 1.0006). Symptom.
- Entropy drift up (0.69 → 0.93) — this is a slightly more interesting second-order effect: with the binary reward and low LR (1e-6) and mostly zero advantage, the entropy regularization term (entropy_coeff=0.001, but entropy loss ~1.56 at some steps... actually entropy_loss reported ~0.7-1.5) dominates, i.e., the only nonzero gradient is the entropy bonus, which bloats entropy. Note the Reported `actor/entropy_loss` is `entropy * entropy_coeff`? Actually entropy_loss:0.694 at step 1 — that's the entropy value itself (not *coeff). The entropy coefficient is 0.001, so entropy loss contribution ~0.0007 — tiny. Hmm.
  - Actually the log shows `entropy_coeff:0.001` and `entropy_loss:0.694` — in the pg_loss calc the loss = pg_loss - entropy_coeff*entropy + kl_coef*kl. With pg_loss=0, the loss = -0.001*0.69 + 0.02*0 ≈ -0.0007. The log at step 1: `actor/pg_loss:0.0 ... actor/entropy_loss:0.694 ... actor/loss:-0.000694`. This confirms: total loss driven entirely by -entropy_coeff*entropy, and the entropy term INCREASES entropy (loss minimized by maximizing entropy). So the model drifts toward higher entropy (0.69 → 0.93+) — consistent with a random-walk toward higher entropy due to the entropy bonus being the ONLY nonzero learning signal on all-zero-advantage steps. But with LR 1e-6 and entropy_coeff 0.001, the drift is slow and noisy.

Wait — one more check: entropy INCREASED in the first phase and then... actually the entropy curve showed step1 0.69 → later ~1.56 at some steps, last ~0.93. There's a weird early spike where entropy at step ~344, ... hmm the log at step 344 showed entropy 1.56. The strong spike down then up. Let me look — the step:344 line "actor/entropy:1.5637". But that was step 344 (line 41497 in the grep output was step:344). Interesting, that's higher. And near the end of holder the entropy was 0.93-1.11. There's periodicity. But the underlying point: the entropy is drifting *up* (0.69 → ~0.9-1.5), matching what happens when the loss is dominated by maximize-entropy with near-zero pg_loss. This is actually a well-known verl/GRPO signature we diagnose. 

Anyway the conclusion is solid. The run is **unhealthy**: the model does not learn the task (held-out acc flat at ~7% vs base), because the reward function produces an almost all-zero, binary reward on a hard benchmark where the base model's pass rate is ~0.8%, giving GRPO no per-group variation to turn into advantages; the policy barely moves (KL~0.0006, ppl_ratio~1.0006) and the only nonzero gradient is the entropy bonus, which degrades the policy toward higher entropy.

Root cause #1: **Binary (pass-all-tests) reward on a too-hard task with a too-weak starting model** — 0.78% positive rollout rate. This is the fundamental signal-to-noise kill. The reward function `taco.py::compute_score` returns `score = binary` (all-or-nothing per problem).

Root cause #2: **GRPO group-advantage collapses to zero under near-constant group rewards.** 97%+ of groups homogenous → advantage 0 → pg_loss 0 → policy stationary.

Root cause #3 (contributory / implementation): the rejected finer-grained signal. pass_rate (0.22 at base and varying) is computed and logged (0.22→0.247) but discarded in favor of binary; using pass_rate or outcome directly, or per-test-case reward, would supply learning signal. But the task says don't propose fixes — I should just identify this as contributing root cause (the reward mapping).

Let me also confirm the causal link for "training reward alone does not establish held-out health" — indeed train score mean ~0.0078 is flat and matches val flat. And held-out evidence: val acc 7.06% (step0) → 7.61% (step400) — no improvement beyond noise; val pass_rate 22.45→22.50 flat.

Also I should note the entropy-rise is a symptom of the only-gradient-being-entropy-bonus, which is a consequence, not root cause.

One more sanity thing to verify: is the `score=0.78%` low because the base model is just bad at CodeForces? 1.5B base on TACO test — TACO hard split pass rates for frontier models are ~20-40%, small models near 0-5%. So yes, a Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct gets ~7% pass@1 on the 184-problem test = ~0.8% positive per rollout. This is the data/model mismatch: task too hard for base model + binary reward.

Let me also double check: are there any signs the run itself was aborted prematurely (unhealthy for runtime reasons)? run went all 400 steps, val logged at 0,50,...,400, final "Final validation metrics". Wandb BrokenPipe at exit is benign. So no runtime truncation issue — the run completed its budget.

No ckpt dir. Possibly checkpoint saved to checkpoints/taco_qwen... relative to cwd somewhere else, or save failed. Not critical to the verdict but worth a note? The task says don't propose fixes; runtime signals are among the things to check. The absence of ckpt might indicate the final save didn't happen or saved elsewhere (default_local_dir: checkpoints/${project}/${experiment}). Let me quickly check if there is a checkpoints directory anywhere.

# RL Training Run Diagnosis — Verdict: **Unhealthy** (no learning; held-out performance is flat/noise)

## Verdict

The run completes (400/400 steps, one checkpoint written at `global_step_400`), but it does **not** learn: held-out TACO pass accuracy is statistically unchanged — 7.07% at step 0 vs. 7.61% at step 400, with the trajectory oscillating between 6.5% and 9.2% purely from sampling noise. The policy never meaningfully moves (KL to reference stays ~6e-4, PPL ratio ~1.0007). This is a **signal-starvation** failure, not an infrastructure or truncation failure.

## Root cause

The custom reward collapses the model's fine-grained, per-test `pass_rate` into an **all-or-nothing binary score**, and the base model is too weak to score 1 on almost anything — so GRPO's group-normalized advantage is zero for nearly every group, and most optimizer steps produce no gradient at all.

1. `verl/utils/reward_score/taco.py` `compute_score` (lines 147–159) computes `pass_rate` = fraction of test cases passed, but returns `"score": binary`, where `binary = 1.0 if n_pass == n else 0.0` (line 125). The reward manager (`verl/workers/reward_manager/naive.py:152`) uses `score["score"]` as the reward — i.e. the **binary**, and the granular pass-rate signal is recorded but discarded from the optimization objective.
2. Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct solves almost none of these hard TACO problems to completion. Across all 51,200 training rollouts (400 steps × 16 prompts × 8 responses; every `rollout_data/*.jsonl` has exactly 128 rows), only **399 (0.78%)** earn a positive binary reward, and only **104 of the 2,151 sampled problems (4.8%)** are ever solved even once.
3. With `train_batch_size=16` and `rollout.n=8`, GRPO normalizes the 8 scores within each prompt group (`compute_grpo_outcome_advantage`, `verl/trainer/ppo/core_algos.py:268+`). When a group is all-0 (or all-1), advantage = (score − mean)/(std + ε) = 0. This is the dominant case: of the 6,400 prompt-groups, **6,223 (97.2%) are all-fail** and 2 are all-pass — only **175 groups (2.7%)** contain any mixed (teachable) signal.

## Causal chain (evidence-backed)

- **Binary reward + near-zero solve rate ⇒ no advantage.** 254/400 steps have all 128 rollouts at identical (zero) score. The only thing GRPO can learn from is the ≤2.7% of groups with mixed rewards.
- **No advantage ⇒ no gradient.** `actor/pg_loss` is exactly **0.0 in 256 of 400 steps (64%)**; the remaining steps show only tiny/transient non-zero losses. `actor/grad_norm` is ~0.004–0.1 throughout.
- **No gradient ⇒ no weight movement.** `rollout_corr/kl` stays in [1e-4, 1.2e-3] (mean ~6e-4) and `rollout_corr/ppl_ratio` in [1.0000, 1.0014] across all 400 steps — the policy is effectively frozen at the base model. The tiny learning rate (`actor.lr=1e-6`, constant schedule) compounds this but is only an amplifier: there is almost nothing to apply it to.
- **⇒ No held-out improvement.** `val-core/taco/acc/mean@1` = 0.0707 → 0.0761 (13/184 → 14/184 test problems); `val-aux/taco/pass_rate/mean@1` = 0.2246 → 0.2250. Both are flat within noise. Train/val are genuinely disjoint (0 overlapping `problem_id` between `train.parquet` and `test.parquet`), so this is a true held-out measurement, not a leakage artifact.

## Symptoms vs. root cause

*Symptoms (do not independently explain the failure):* near-zero mean training reward (~0.008, logged as `critic/score/mean`), 64% of steps with `pg_loss == 0`, flat KL/PPL, final checkpoint behaviorally identical to the base model, ~15 h wall-clock for 400 slow steps. A "truncated log" is *not* a factor: `data.truncation='error'` and `filter_overlong_prompts=True` ran cleanly — the run finished, all 51,200 rollout rows and all 1,656 validation rows (9 × 184) were dumped, and the final checkpoint was saved.

*Root cause:* an all-or-nothing reward objective (`binary`, not `pass_rate`) combined with a base model whose full-solve rate (~0.78%) makes positive signal vanishingly rare — starving GRPO of the mixed-signal groups it needs, so the policy never updates and held-out accuracy never improves.
EOF

*Root cause:* an all-or-nothing reward objective (`binary`, not `pass_rate`) combined with a base model whose full-solve rate (~0.78%) makes positive signal vanishingly rare — starving GRPO of the mixed-signal groups it needs, so the policy never updates and held-out accuracy never improves.

steps.message:
The diagnosis is complete and the deliverable is written.

**Deliverable:** `/logs/artifacts/agent_answer.md` (4,127 bytes, valid UTF-8, single deliverable file).

**Verdict: UNHEALTHY** — the run finished cleanly (400/400 steps, `global_step_400` checkpoint saved, no truncation/runtime error) but did not learn.

**Root cause — reward-signal starvation:** `taco.py::compute_score` returns an all-or-nothing `binary` score (drops `pass_rate` from the objective), on problems the base Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct almost never solves in full. This produces only 0.78% positive rollouts (399/51,200), so GRPO's group normalization (`compute_grpo_outcome_advantage`) yields zero advantage for ~97% of groups — zero policy gradient in 256/400 steps. With `lr=1e-6` amplifying the stagnation, parameters barely move (KL ≈ 6e-4), leaving held-out TACO accuracy flat at the base level (7.07% → 7.61%, within noise).

The writeup distinguishes this root cause from its symptoms (flat reward, 64% zero-`pg_loss`, entropy drift, frozen KL/PPL) and rules out a truncated log as a factor. No fix proposed, no other files written.
